lessons.title: മുൻപ് (munpŭ) — before
lessons.gloss: before — a word that stands after the thing it is before, on an ending you already build

segments.text: Say at two o'clock. Then say the word you have for then — the one that puts one turn after another.
മുൻപ് (munpŭ) — before.
It goes after. English puts before in front of what it is before; Malayalam puts it behind:
രണ്ട് മണിക്ക് മുൻപ് — raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ — "before two o'clock."
Read that right to left and it comes out as English: before — two o'clock.

Look at what it is standing on. മണിക്ക് — the hour with the dative on it, exactly as you built it. മുൻപ് (munpŭ) does not attach to the word and does not change it. It is a separate word that leans on an ending you already make.
The word itself is built on mun, the old Dravidian word for the front. What is in front of you in space became what is in front of you in time.

segments.instruction: which word carries the ending, and which one leans on it
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which word carries the ending, and which one leans on it]

segments.text: Before two o'clock? (രണ്ട് മണിക്ക് മുൻപ് (munpŭ).) Where does മുൻപ് (munpŭ) stand — in front of the hour or after it? (After it.) What is it built on? (mun, the word for the front.)

lessons.title: ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) — after
lessons.gloss: after — the partner of before, standing in the same place on the same ending

segments.text: Say before two o'clock. Then say the word for the meal.
ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) — after.
It stands where മുൻപ് (munpŭ) stands, on the same kind of ending:
ഊണിന് ശേഷം — ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ — "after the meal."

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: the same case, wearing its other shape

segments.text: ഊണിന് is the dative again — and it is the other of the two shapes you were given. The hour took -ക്ക്; ഊണ് takes -ിന്, because the ending is chosen by the sound the word finishes on.

utterances: രണ്ട് മണിക്ക് മുൻപ്, raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ, before two o'clock.
ഊണിന് ശേഷം, ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ, after the meal.

segments.text: Same case, two shapes, and both of these words lean on it. You are not learning a new piece of machinery — you are hanging two more words on a piece you have had since your first case ending.
ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) is Sanskrit, and its plain meaning is the remainder — what is left over. After the meal is, in the word's own terms, what is left of the day once the meal is done.

segments.instruction: raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ, then ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ — and name the two shapes of the one ending
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ*, then *ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ* — and name the two shapes of the one ending]

segments.text: After the meal? (ഊണിന് ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ).) Which two shapes of the dative did this chapter use? (-ക്ക് on the hour, -ിന് on the meal.) What does ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) plainly mean? (The remainder — what is left over.)

lessons.title: ആദ്യം, പിന്നെ, മുൻപ് (munpŭ), ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) — two kinds of ordering
lessons.gloss: first, then, before, after — two words that order turns and two that order events, and the difference between them

segments.text: Say at first. Say then. You have had both for a long while.
You now have four words about order, and they split into two pairs that do different jobs.

utterances: ആദ്യം, പിന്നെ, ādyaṁ, pinne, stand alone and order the telling.
മുൻപ്, ശേഷം, munpŭ, śēṣaṁ, lean on a word and order events.

segments.text: ആദ്യം and പിന്നെ need nothing in front of them. They say first this, then that about the order you are saying things in.
മുൻപ് (munpŭ) and ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) cannot stand alone. Each one needs a thing to be before or after, and that thing arrives wearing the dative.

segments.instruction: ādyaṁ, then pinne — ordering the telling
raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ — ordering an event against an hour
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ* — ordering an event against an hour]

segments.instruction: ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ — ordering an event against a meal
segments.source: [YOU SAY: *ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ* — ordering an event against a meal]

segments.instruction: which two of the four could be said with nothing else beside them
segments.source: [YOU SAY: which two of the four could be said with nothing else beside them]

segments.text: Until this chapter you could order your own sentences and not the world. First … then … arranges what you say. Before two o'clock and after the meal arrange what happens, against something you name.
That is the whole of what the two new words add — and neither of them needed a new piece of grammar to do it.
Which two of the four stand alone? (ആദ്യം and പിന്നെ.) Which two need something to lean on? (മുൻപ് (munpŭ) and ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ).) What does the thing they lean on wear? (The dative.)

lessons.title: (before, after) (munpuṁ śēṣavuṁ enna ōrmma) — from cold
lessons.gloss: cold retrieval of the two words that order events, and of the ending they both lean on

segments.text: Close the lessons before this one. Say before and after.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: both of them lean, and neither of them attaches

utterances: രണ്ട് മണിക്ക് മുൻപ്, raṇṭŭ maṇikkŭ munpŭ, before two o'clock.
ഊണിന് ശേഷം, ūṇinŭ śēṣaṁ, after the meal.

segments.text: Neither word changed the word in front of it. The hour is the hour you already built; the meal is the meal with the dative's other shape on it. Both new words are separate, and both stand behind what they are about — which is the opposite of where English puts them.

The ending underneath both of them is your first case ending. It was glossed to and for; you put it on an hour to mean at; and now two more words lean on it. One ending, four jobs, and no new machinery in this chapter at all.
And you can now order two different things: ആദ്യം and പിന്നെ order the telling, മുൻപ് (munpŭ) and ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ) order the events.

segments.instruction: where these two stand, compared with where English puts them
segments.source: [YOU SAY: where these two stand, compared with where English puts them]

segments.text: Before two o'clock? (രണ്ട് മണിക്ക് മുൻപ് (munpŭ).) After the meal? (ഊണിന് ശേഷം (śēṣaṁ).) Do they go in front of the thing or behind it? (Behind.)
